guard_inputs:
# The files the guard suite (hooks/test_guard.py and tests/guard/*.py, run in the checks-windows-guard shards) reads. ci-scope.sh
# turns windows_guard on when a diff touches a path that matches a line here, so the Windows guard shards run for that diff only.
# One glob per line; `*` also matches `/`. A `#` starts a comment. An empty or unreadable list turns the shards on for every diff.
# lint/test_guard_inputs.py checks the list against the files the suite opens, names and imports.
hooks/*
tests/guard/*
agents/*
lint/*
janitor/*
merge/*
testing/*
skills/waiting-page/*
settings.json
install.sh
package.json
landed-dirs.txt
docs/decisions/agent-model-cap.md
docs/decisions/brief-ids-in-roster.md
skills/impeccable/SKILL.md
bin/lane-start
bin/sim-lease
bin/sim-test
actions/ci-alarm/events.json
actions/ci-alarm/clear_rule.py
.github/stamp.json
.claude/layout-extras.json
package-lock.json
landed: # Directories that install.sh and install.ps1 land under ~/.claude (or %USERPROFILE%\.claude).
# One directory name per line. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
# This file is the single source for both installers. install.sh reads it once. install.ps1
# reads it twice: once for its own foreach, once inside the embedded post-merge hook it writes,
# so a `git pull` on a symlink-less machine lands the same set.
# hooks/guard.py keeps CONFIG_FROZEN_DIRS as its own literal on purpose. See the comment beside
# it in hooks/guard.py for why a frozen-path list must never be read from a file at runtime.
# lint/check_landed_dirs.py checks that the two stay in agreement, `state` excepted: it is a
# guard-only extra, never landed by either installer.
